title: Typing NestJS patterns
subtitle: DTO classes, pipes, guards, decorators, config

cards.front: Why Nest DTOs are classes, not interfaces?
cards.meaning: Interfaces and types erase. Decorators like @IsEmail() need a runtime target so metadata can attach via reflect-metadata. A class compiles to a constructor, so it is both the compile-time type and the runtime validation source of truth. ValidationPipe reads that metadata; an interface leaves nothing to decorate.

cards.front: What shape is an HTTP body before ValidationPipe?
cards.meaning: A plain object, untrusted. Types on @Body() do not make it a validated instance by themselves.

cards.front: What is the ValidationPipe DTO pipeline?
cards.meaning: HTTP body arrives as a plain object. With transform: true, class-transformer instantiates the DTO class. class-validator reads decorator metadata and validates. The controller then receives a typed DTO instance, or Nest throws 400.
cards.example: app.useGlobalPipes(new ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, transform: true }));

cards.front: What does ValidationPipe transform: true do?
cards.meaning: It turns the plain JSON object into a real class instance via class-transformer, so decorator metadata and validation run on a CreateUserDto, not a leftover POJO.

cards.front: What does ValidationPipe whitelist: true do?
cards.meaning: It strips properties without decorator metadata, which helps block unexpected fields from reaching persistence.
cards.notes: Skipping whitelist is a common mistake — extra body keys can be accepted.

cards.front: Does @Body() dto: CreateUserDto validate without a pipe?
cards.meaning: No. Without the pipe plus a class DTO, dto: CreateUserDto is only a TypeScript annotation — erasure means nothing validates at runtime.

cards.front: Is Omit<User,'passwordHash'> enough to hide a hash in JSON?
cards.meaning: No. Compile-time Omit only constrains what you write in TS. If you return userEntity, Nest JSON-serializes the real object and passwordHash can still leak. Type safety is not an output filter. Safer: a response DTO class plus ClassSerializerInterceptor with @Exclude() / @Expose().
Generics keep roles distinct: CreateUserDto is inbound and validated, User/entity is persistence, UserResponseDto is outbound safe fields. Avoid one any-ish “user” object for the whole stack.

cards.front: Repository<User> — what is User at runtime?
cards.meaning: The generic parameter is the entity class — a runtime construct for the ORM — separate from HTTP DTO classes used at the boundary.

cards.front: How should createParamDecorator be typed for CurrentUser?
cards.meaning: Give the factory a return type of User so controllers receive a documented type, not any. The decorator only reads request.user — a guard or middleware must set it, and Express declaration merging makes Request.user known to TS.
cards.example: export const CurrentUser = createParamDecorator((data: unknown, ctx: ExecutionContext): User => { ... return request.user as User; });

cards.front: What goes wrong if @CurrentUser() is typed User but no guard sets req.user?
cards.meaning: The type lies. Without a guard or middleware assigning request.user, you get a typed hole at runtime. Pair the decorator with a guard that sets user and with Request.user augmentation.

cards.front: What does a Nest guard implement?
cards.meaning: CanActivate — implement canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): boolean | Promise<boolean>. Return true to allow, false or throw to block.
An abstract wrapper around the current request. Use switchToHttp() (or rpc/ws) and type getRequest<Request>() so req is not any. Guards are not untyped Express middleware.

intercept(context: ExecutionContext, next: CallHandler) returns Observable. next.handle() is the handler result stream. Map/transform here, or use ClassSerializerInterceptor for DTO serialization. You do not need deep RxJS — know the wrap-before-and-after shape.

cards.front: Does config.get<number>('PORT') parse the env value?
cards.meaning: No. get<T> is a type-assertion-shaped generic — it does not coerce strings from env. Use transform in config validation (Joi/Zod/class-validator) for real parsing. Omitting <T> often leaves values loosely typed.
get<T>(key) is typically T | undefined. getOrThrow<T>(key) is for keys that must exist, e.g. getOrThrow<string>('DATABASE_URL').
